purpose: Split settings status into Saved vs Verified with cause-class diagnostics and a keyless trial preview to fix verify-but-not-persist confusion.
riskRationale: Probe boolean behavior is preserved and credential handling stays blind, but new Settings-to-probe delegation adds a partial-SDK fatal surface and version-sync hard rule is violated.

text: The PR implements what it claims: shared cached probe backing isConfigured/diagnose, Saved vs Verified UI, cause diagnostics, and a keyless preview, all credential-blind with clean escaping. It should not merge yet: versions are out of sync (@since 0.1.5 vs 0.1.4 with no readme bump), the Settings validCauses guard is incomplete against the uncatchable-trait fatal it cites, and the new cause/marker/preview paths have no test coverage.

reasoning: Version-sync hard rule violated and the anti-fatal guard for the new Settings→Availability delegation is incomplete; both must be fixed plus tests for the new diagnostics paths.

message: Bust closures take zero parameters and only delete plugin-owned transients plus set a timestamp marker, preserving the credential-blind hard rule (no connectors_ai_* reads/writes).
Single shared probe() backs both isConfigured() and diagnose() with one TTL for verdict+cause, so diagnostics add zero extra HTTP as claimed.
Stale-cache migration (verdict without cause falls back to ok/unknown) keeps 0.1.4 installs working after upgrade.
All user-facing output is escaped (esc_html/esc_url/wp_kses_post) and the dry-run filter output is escaped, so no XSS or key disclosure surface.
Defensive SDK entry-point probing with fail-open to network-failure instead of fataling is thorough and well-commented (including the magic-enum caveat).

validCauses() guard is incomplete against the uncatchable fatal it cites: it checks ProviderAvailabilityInterface + WithHttpTransporterTrait but not WithRequestAuthenticationTrait, so a partial SDK (transporter present, auth trait missing) still fatals inside class_exists(OpenCodeProviderAvailability::class).
suggestion: Add the missing trait_exists check for WithRequestAuthenticationTrait (the second trait used by the availability class) before touching the class.

message: Version-sync hard rule violated: new APIs are tagged @since 0.1.5 but Version header, VERSION const, and readme.txt Stable tag all remain 0.1.4 with no Changelog/Upgrade Notice entry.
suggestion: Either bump to 0.1.5 everywhere (Version header, VERSION const, readme Stable tag + Changelog entry) or revert the @since tags to 0.1.4.

message: No test coverage for the new behavior: diagnose()/validCauses()/causeMessage()/dryRunPreview()/isSaveReverted, the go_cause/zen_cause deletes, or the key_seen markers. The existing bust test does not assert cause deletes or marker writes, so regressions in the headline feature are invisible.
suggestion: Extend SlimBustHooksTest to stub set_transient/get_transient and assert both cause transients are deleted and the per-catalog key_seen marker is written; add unit tests for causeMessage mapping and diagnosisFor override logic.

message: Stale @throws RuntimeException docblock on probe(): every code path returns an array and all WP/SDK/HTTP calls are wrapped in try/catch, so probe() never throws.
suggestion: Remove the @throws line from probe() docblock (keep try/catch in callers as belt-and-braces).

message: diagnosisFor() defaults a live-configured result with no cached cause to 'ok', collapsing throttled/valid-no-credits precision, and can render Verified: connected alongside a Status-unknown message.
suggestion: Default to 'unknown' with a live-configured override only when a cached cause is absent, or keep the boolean from the registry without forcing the cause to ok.

message: HTTP 403 is unconditionally mapped to bad-key, but 403 can also mean geo-block, IP policy, or moderation rather than an invalid key, which would misdirect users to re-enter a valid key.
suggestion: Qualify the 403 mapping (e.g. only bad-key with an auth-shaped error body, else unknown) or document why all 403s are treated as key failures.

message: dryRunPreview() gates on WordPress >= 7.0, which is always true given Requires at least: 7.0, making the unsupported branch dead code on supported installs.
suggestion: Document the gate as forward-compat hardening or simplify it away; no behavior change needed.

message: Inconsistent fail-open guards in the bust closure: avail verdict deletes are unguarded while cause deletes and marker writes are function_exists/try-catch guarded, so a bare-PHP (no-WP) context fatals on the first two lines but survives the rest.
suggestion: Wrap the first two delete_transient calls in the same function_exists guard for consistency.
